text:
Predicates:
RankedHighly(x) ::: x is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
ActivePlayer(x) ::: x is one of the most active players in major tennis.
LostTo(x, y) ::: x lost to y.
IgaSwiatek(x) ::: x is Iga Świątek.
RolandGarras2022(x) ::: x participated in Roland Garros 2022.
Female(x) ::: x is a female tennis player.
Male(x) ::: x is a male tennis player.
AtEvent(x, y) ::: x participated in event y.
---

Premises:
∀x (RankedHighly(x) → ActivePlayer(x)) ::: If someone is ranked highly by WTA, then they are one of the most active players.
∀x (LostTo(x, IgaSwiatek) → RankedHighly(x)) ::: Everyone who lost to Iga Świątek is ranked highly.
∀x (AtEvent(x, RolandGarras2022) ∧ Female(x)) → LostTo(x, IgaSwiatek) ::: All female players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Iga Świątek.
∀x (AtEvent(x, RolandGarras2022)) → (Female(x) ∨ Male(x)) ::: All players at Roland Garros 2022 are either female or male.
∀x (Male(x) ∧ AtEvent(x, RolandGarras2022)) → LostTo(x, RafaelNadal) ::: All male players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Rafael Nadal.
---

Conclusion:
(RankedHighly(CocoGauff) ∨ LostTo(CocoGauff, RafaelNadal)) → ¬Male(CocoGauff) ::: If Coco Gauff is either ranked highly or lost to Rafael Nadal, then she is not a male player at Roland Garros 2022.
